en.question: What is the custard tart sold in almost every Portuguese café called in Portuguese?
en.fact: The recipe is said to come from the monks of the Jerónimos Monastery in Lisbon's Belém district. The bakery next door has sold them since 1837.

es.question: ¿Cómo se llama en portugués la tartaleta de crema que venden en casi todos los cafés de Portugal?
es.fact: Se dice que la receta viene de los monjes del Monasterio de los Jerónimos, en el barrio lisboeta de Belém. La pastelería de al lado los vende desde 1837.

en.question: In Portugal, what does a woman say to say "thank you"?
en.fact: It literally means "obliged", so it matches the speaker: men say obrigado, women say obrigada.

en.question: What is the name of Portugal's famous mournful style of music, often heard in Lisbon's taverns?
en.fact: UNESCO declared fado part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2011.

en.question: What number is the famous yellow tram that rattles through Graça, Alfama and Estrela in Lisbon?
en.fact: Many of Lisbon's trams are vintage cars from the 1930s, rebuilt and still in daily service.

en.question: What is the Portuguese name for the salted dried cod found on almost every menu?
en.fact: The Portuguese say there's a bacalhau recipe for every day of the year, yet most of the cod is imported from Norway.

en.question: What is the tax number every resident needs in Portugal, and gets asked for at the till, called?
en.fact: Giving your NIF when you pay registers the receipt with the tax office, which can earn you deductions on your income tax.

en.question: In what year did the great earthquake destroy much of Lisbon?
en.fact: It struck on 1 November. The quake, a tsunami and fires that burned for days levelled much of the city.
